title: Zesty Herb Chinese Sea Bass Cha Siu Bao
description: Tender and flavorful dish featuring sea bass, fines-herbes, and a hint of Chinese five-spice. Serve in a delicate char siu bao bun.

ingredients.name: fines-herbes (such as parsley, chives, and dill)

instructions: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil for easy cleanup.
Rinse the sea bass fillets under cold water, pat dry with paper towels, and season with salt.
In a small bowl, mix together the fines-herbes, garlic, ginger, five-spice powder, soy sauce, brown sugar, and rice vinegar.
Pour the marinade over the sea bass fillets, turning to coat evenly.
Transfer the sea bass fillets to the prepared baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes, or until cooked through.
Meanwhile, split the cha siu bao buns in half horizontally and toast until lightly browned.
To assemble the dish, place a cooked sea bass fillet in each bun half, spoon some of the pan juices over the top, and garnish with chopped green onions.
Serve immediately, with additional fines-herbes and green onions on the side if desired.
To make the tagine, heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add the cooked sea bass fillets to the saucepan and simmer in the tagine for 2-3 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened.
Strain the tagine through a fine-mesh sieve into a small bowl, discarding the solids.
Serve the tagine over the sea bass fillets in the cha siu bao buns.
